_comment: SHARED UI-element library for flicker clients: a flat map of named UI-element definitions, loaded into a ScriptHost and exposed to Lua as the `UI` global; each client's scripts read the elements they need by name (unused keys are ignored). Front-end shell (inherited by every client): `modal` (shared component style) + `screens.*` (its instances, selected by Model.screen) + `settings` + `logo` + `loading`. Per-client in-game HUDs are added here too, keyed by element name: `hud` = flicker-csg. Colors are RGBA 0..1; positions/sizes are HUD pixels; `texture` names resolve through the `Textures` global. COLOURS ARE THE PRISM DESIGN LANGUAGE: every colour is a `$token` reference into `theme.tokens` (the single palette source), expanded by the load_ui_json resolver before the tree reaches Lua — never hardcode an rgba here, add/point a token. As more clients migrate, add their HUD element(s) here — namespace the key if it would collide (e.g. two clients both wanting `hud`).
_bucket_palette: ══ PALETTE ══  The single Prism token source. Every colour in this file is a $token ref resolved against theme.tokens by flicker-widgets::resolve_tokens before the tree reaches Lua — so the palette MUST stay in the same root as everything referencing it.

theme._comment: The Prism palette — the ONE source of UI colour (imported from the 'Prism UI Design Language': cold carved stone lit by sapphire rune-light, aged bronze the only structural metal, the 7-colour Septisigil for stats). Every colour elsewhere in this file is a `$name` reference resolved against this map. Stone ramp = surfaces (dark→light); edge = borders; ink/dim/faint = text; bronze = structural metal; sap_* = the interactive/live accent (base/hover/pressed + border + glow); rune_glow = lit text/focus; hp/mana/stam = resource ramps; sig_* = the seven stat colours. Derived translucent tokens (sheen/scrim/wash/panel_bg/hairline/cell_hot) are alpha variants of the same palette.

_stages_comment: STAGE SOURCES — named offscreen sub-scenes (RTT) that a `stage` UI node composites into its rect. A source says WHAT to render (lighting preset, camera, content layers); the NODE says WHERE it lands (its rect + its `panel` style, which the walker draws as the backdrop). Draw ORDER is deliberately NOT expressed here: flicker-render::FrameGraph derives it topologically and must execute() first thing in render(). Layers carry only scalars, $token colours and *_bind Model keys — never geometry — so the data-only script boundary holds. The `lighting` presets are salvaged from the retired packeditor (pip_scene / night_scene).

portrait._comment: One character on a dark void — the Loomforge Stage doll (pack cards, clip rows, creature roster + hero). The node's panel style supplies the backdrop gradient, so the target clears TRANSPARENT and the doll composites over it.

turntable._comment: Wider framing over a ground grid — the TAE editor preview (300px) and any full-body review shot.

sablework_lit._comment: The Sablework LIT PREVIEW — the material shown on a turning sample under a fixed light, which is the only way roughness/metalness/normal relief actually read. The `material` layer is drawn by the bench's own lit module (it binds the six preview maps it already holds); the target clears TRANSPARENT so the node's panel supplies the backdrop, matching `portrait`.

godmode_globe._comment: The God Mode GLOBE — the forming planet, drawn into the bench's centre viewport. Deliberately has NO `camera` block, and that absence is a decision rather than an omission: every other stage frames a fixed subject, but this one is flown by the maintainer, so the scene's own orbit camera owns the view and the stage authors only the light it is seen by and the backdrop it sits on. `clear` is transparent so the node's `rtt_holder` panel shows through, matching `sablework_lit`.

pocepochs_globe._comment: The PLANET SIMULATION globe — the forward-regenerative epoch sim's world. Like `godmode_globe` it publishes its own shells (the surface shell, or the classified per-column layer stack) and authors no `camera`, because the planet is flown by the maintainer. `clear` is transparent so the scene's own deep-space backdrop shows through the composited viewport.

populous_globe._comment: The POPULOUS hex ledger globe — the authored world drawn into the multi-view's centre viewport. Like `godmode_globe` it deliberately has NO `camera` block: the map is flown by the game master, so the scene's own orbit camera owns the view and the stage authors only the light it is seen by (the default light source). `clear` is transparent so the node's holder panel shows through. Unlike God Mode, this world has NO simulation publishing shells, so its whole appearance is authored here: the near-black under-shell, the inset tile shell over it (the seams between the tiles show the shell beneath, and those seams ARE the outlines — two static shells, no per-edge line geometry), and the shared reference frame above both.

_bucket_shell: ══ SHELL CHROME ══  Front-end shell (Alpha/crates/frontend/flicker-shell), embedded via include_str! and inherited by every client: modal + screens (its instances) + menu + settings + logo + loading. Scripts: menu.lua, settings.lua, logo.lua.
_modal_comment: Prism carved-stone modal, drawn (not baked): the shared style for the main menu / pause 'Sanctum' / display-confirm — declared by menu.lua (`MENU.screen` picks the form) through the `popup_panel`/`popup_menu`/`choice_dialog` templates and rendered by the component walker. Chrome = `panel` HudCommands (rounded-rect + 2-stop gradient + border); buttons pick a `variant` (primary sapphire / secondary stone / danger rust). The panel auto-sizes to its content, so a screen just lists its title/subtitle/items. Sizes are px; every colour a `$token`.
_menu_comment: Scene-selection LAUNCHER styling (menu.lua, when MENU.scene_select): the right scene panel + its data-driven rows (bronze preview frame, mode/name/desc/meta text) and the backdrop scrim fade + prism thread. Reuses modal.* for the popup + buttons. Colours are $tokens or literal rgba.
_settings_comment: Prism Settings 'workbench' (settings.lua): a resizable window (capped to the viewport) = title bar + left category rail (Video/Audio/Input, each keyed to a Septisigil gem) + right scrolling content + footer (Restore / Back / Apply). Chrome + controls are VECTOR `panel` commands. Controls carry `wired`: true = bound to the shell settings/input backend, false = an inert layout preview (FOV, brightness, edge-pan, all of Audio, the controller device — no engine behind them yet). Every colour is a $token.

titlebar._fill_note: fill_top/fill_bot = the declared `wash` so draw_panel_bg actually tints the bar (was falling back to the dark PANEL constant); `color` = `title_color` so the title text picks it up (draw_text reads `color`/`label_color`, not `title_color`).
titlebar.title: $set_settings

rebind_banner.text2: Esc to cancel · Backspace to unbind

_controller_tier_comment: CONTROLLER TIER. `pad_glyphs` is the ONE description of the input-hint atlas — which texture, the grid, and the name → 0-based cell map — read by the engine's button glyph face (`draw_glyph_face` in component.rs; a node passes `glyph_style: "pad_glyphs"`) and by nothing else. The sheet (Alpha/content/package/sensorium/assets/prism_pad_glyphs.png) and this map are generated together by tools/gen_prism_pad_glyphs.py from the source SVGs in content/source/prism_ui_icons: regenerate and re-edit together, and APPEND only — inserting a glyph renumbers every cell after it. `tex` is the id `Theme::lua_textures()` registers the atlas at (white 0, muse 1, pad_glyphs 2). Glyphs are baked white with the shape in alpha, so `color` here IS the appearance. `paged_menu` styles the controller-first page/tab surface: `hint` is the resting shoulder chip, `hint_on` the lit one, `page_*` the LT/RT rail, `tab_*` the LB/RB pill rail, `well`/`row` the content columns, `legend_*` the footer.
_hud_tier_comment: GAME-HUD TIER (DS components/game realized as walker kinds). resource_gauge: one block, per-tone fill keys picked by the node's `tone` prop (badge precedent); track/border shared; `low` state swaps border + label. action_slot: 58px hotbar recess (DS --slot-size), rune glyph + keybind + charges + cooldown veil, `active` lights the sapphire ring. medallion: SDF-circle ring portrait — ring variants nested under `rings` (metal gradient pairs); rune fallback glyph over the dark gem well. stat_dot: septisigil gem-dot, hues nested under `hues` (fill + glow pairs from the sig_* ramp).

unit_frame._comment: The unit_frame TEMPLATE's chrome (ui_templates.json): `card` for friendly/self, `hostile` tints the slab blood. name_color/subtitle_color are text colour leaves; the block itself styles the row cell.

workflow._comment: The workflow proto's shared chrome (ui_templates.json `workflow` + the flicker-widgets runtime). `chip` styles are the rail states the runtime publishes as style_bind paths (workflow.chip.active/visited/todo) — one palette, every bench.

rtt_holder._comment: The framed RTT HOLDER the `rtt_panel` proto defaults to, and every bench's RTT slot styles against — the template-tier namespace for an offscreen-view slot's chrome (replaced the per-scene assetpipeline holder block, same values).

_slider_comment: THE SLIDER SKIN - the `slider` component's one template-tier palette, worn by the `pop_size_dial` proto and by any slider that is not a bench's own instrument. Resting track/fill/handle plus the FOCUSED trio the component swaps in while the walker's cursor is on it (`focus_track` / `focus_fill` / `focus_label`), and the type sizes the value readout and the label draw at. A scene never passes a slider style: the proto names this block, and a bench-namespaced copy (`sablework.slider`, `assetpipeline.slider`) is a bench's own instrument panel, never the default.
_panel_comment: THE PANEL SKIN - the `panel` component's own two states, and the ONE pane palette every multi-panel view wears (ui_panel, rtt_panel, and the tri-pane's side panes). `resting` is what a pane looks like; `focused` carries the sapphire rim the walker puts on the pane holding the panel cursor (on a pad this ring IS the cursor's home). There is no per-bench pane palette and no scene-passed rim: the WALKER owns which panel is focused, the PANEL owns what that looks like. The whole `tri_pane` block folded in here - its five pane skins collapsed to these two (the entered tier died with the enter/exit mode), and its `empty` placeholder ink plus the `stat_label`/`stat_value` caption/data inks came along. Every colour a $token.
_bucket_scenes: ══ SCENE HUDS ══  One namespaced section per live scene, read by that scene's crate plus Alpha/content/scripts/hud_<scene>.lua. Kept alphabetical: ADD A NEW SCENE AS A NEW KEY HERE — never a second file, which would fork the palette.

assetpipeline._comment: Asset Pipeline editor (flicker-assetpipeline) — the in-app content-pipeline wizard. Built to DesignSync project 2fc44682 'Asset Pipeline.dc.html'. Colours are $token refs resolved against this file's theme.tokens — the ONE Prism palette; never a private copy.
assetpipeline._map_comment: BONE-MAP / REQUIREMENT COLOUR KEY — the one place the conform provenance states get their colour. ok = a source bone renamed to canonical; review = placed by a derive pass (hip/shoulder/ankle) and worth a human's eye; auto = inferred from the reference rig; fail = a Review requirement that is not met. Bound per-row as a dotted path via `<row>_color`, so the key cannot drift between the list and the summary.
assetpipeline._choice_comment: An EXCLUSIVE-CHOICE row and a LIST-SELECTION row. Both are `button`s: exclusivity is state the engine already owns, so a radio needs no component of its own — the caption arrives by text_bind carrying the selected glyph. `choice` is a flat stone row; `rowsel` is the selected-row marker the design specifies (a sapphire accent wash) and draws NOTHING when a row is unselected, so it sits under a bound text without covering it.
assetpipeline._import_comment: IMPORT WORKFLOW SELECTOR (Step::Task) — the standard Prism `window` template (a PRESET over `frame`: chiseled `settings.window` border + automatic glowing CORNER RUNES + an 'Import' title bar), sized RESPONSIVELY at `win_frac` of the screen, its `content` slot holding the reusable `option_grid` selector field (heading · sunk well of a flowing card grid · hint), `cols`-per-row for an ARBITRARY workflow count. `card` is the transparent CLICK+HOVER overlay over each tile: idle shows the $edge3 resting edge; hover lights the Prism-DS 'selected ring' ($sapphire border + $sap_glow halo) plus a faint $accent_wash. `import.*` sizes: `win_frac` the window size, `head_size` the title glyph; `sec_/subtitle_/hint_size` the field's heading/subtitle/hint; `grid_*` the grid + well; `card_size`/`pad`/`gap`/`slot_h`/`rune_size`/`title_*`/`desc_*`/`tag_*` each square tile (the italic flavour WRAPS to the card width over its `desc_h`). Tiles carry NO Model label — copy/runes are static instance params on the `clayworks_import_card` proto.
assetpipeline._workbench_comment: KILNWORKS WORKBENCH CHROME — a solid TILED layout (not floating overlays): a full-bleed `header` bar filling the top, a `tab_bar` of the six pipeline steps drawn Loomforge-style (NON-interactive — the active step lights via the walker's `style_bind`; the footer Back/Next drives the step), a `body` row holding the framed RTT `holder` (the 2×2 editor viewport) beside a first-class editor rail (`inspector`), and a full-bleed `footer`. `tab_bar`/`tab_active`/`tab_idle` intentionally mirror `loomforge.tab_*` (same $tokens, no hover — the tabs don't respond to the pointer); DEDUP: promote to a shared component block when the design-system component tier lands.
assetpipeline._stage_comment: PER-STAGE INSPECTOR CONTROLS — one block per wizard step, each shown only while its `on_<step>` flag is set. `rig` = the inline piece picker (multi-mesh folders) + the paged bone map (`rows` must equal the crate's BONE_ROWS) + the four offset sliders, whose ±range lives HERE so Rust and Lua cannot disagree about it; `attach` = the six socket rows + three offset sliders; `review` = the requirement rows (`rows` must equal REQUIREMENT_ROWS) + the commit button.

clicktrainer._comment: flicker-clicktrainer in-game HUD (hud_clicktrainer.lua): a DECLARATIVE walker tree — a vector stats panel over the 2D sprite target, the reference blend of VECTOR UI + a 2D SPRITE GAME + CLICK ROUTING. The walker reports `hud_hit` so a click on the panel is a UI click (RESET), never scored as a game miss. Stat values flow from the scene via Model as pre-formatted text.

chemistry._comment: flicker-godmode / God Mode HUD (composition lives in ui_templates.json as the godmode_* protos): the walker readout — loading banner, title/stats/interior/state/crust lines, and the text-only CONSERVATION LEDGER panel (top-right). The seed-element swatch panel + tectonic-event log stay scene-drawn (data-driven literal colours have no walker channel). Colours are $tokens where the legacy literals matched; the rest are the POC's own readout palette, kept verbatim.

loomforge._comment: Loomforge Bench (crates/flicker-loomforge) — the animation-authoring editor: State Machine · Pack Browser · Creature Composer · TAE Editor. The chrome (top bar / tab bar / body) is a Rust UiNode tree run through the flicker-widgets walker; the node-graph canvas and TAE timeline are drawn by the scene itself. Every colour is a $token ref into theme.tokens — the one Prism palette.
loomforge._canvas_comment: The node-graph canvas is drawn by the SCENE (not the widgets walker), so it reads these colours by dotted path rather than as a node style.
loomforge._stage_comment: Backdrop panels for `stage` nodes. The doll composites INTO the rect these frame; `inset` is how far the image sits inside the border. What each stage RENDERS lives in the shared top-level `stages` block, named by the node's `source` prop.
loomforge._pack_kind_comment: Pack Browser accent per pack KIND. The kind is DERIVED by reading what a pack contains (combat windows -> Weapon, events -> Ability, multi-state and eventless -> Locomotion), never authored into the file — there is no gameplay runtime behind a pack category yet, so no pack claims one. Hexes are the DC's: #9db8ff / #c8707a / #e0b23a / #8f8a7d, each an EXACT existing token.
loomforge._tae_lane_comment: The nine TAE event lanes, keyed by lane id — their ORDER lives in Rust (tae::Lane::ALL), because order is spec, not colour. Per lane: `swatch` tints the gutter label, `row`/`row_border` are the track's own fill and edge, `event` fills a window bar. A one-shot (an event with no `end` tick) draws as a narrow marker in the same colour, so point-vs-span comes from the DATA rather than from which lane it lands on.

paperdoll._comment: flicker-paperdoll's in-scene HUD (behaviour: Alpha/content/scripts/hud_paperdoll.lua). Replaces the POC keypress toggles + draw_text overlay. `inventory` = the equip-slot bar; a slot's piece is drawn only while its cell is lit. Slot keys are the contract with the engine: it publishes `slot_<key>_loaded`/`slot_<key>_on` on the Model and reads `slot_<key>` back. Sheaths have no cell by design — they are always worn (no sheath/unsheath animations yet).

view._items_note: `animate` = the Animation/Pose toggle: on drives the pose from the pack's state machine (real runtime animation, blended), off is A-pose/bind (the fitting reference — Idle is an authored stance, already off bind). ↑/↓ cycle animation states, Space pauses. `blend` A/Bs the transition crossfade.

fit._comment: The fit gadget — shown only while a piece is selected (Model.fit_active). Click a piece in the scene to select it; click empty space to deselect. `offset` sliders are in WORLD axes at rest (x lateral, y depth, z up), NOT bone axes — the torso bones are tilted 90°, so bone-space nudging would be unusable by eye. Record writes every loaded piece's fit to musefit/fits.json.
fit._focus_note: Click a slider to FOCUS it; ←/→ then nudge it by `nudge` (hold Shift for `nudge_coarse`). A trackpad drag over a ~120px track spans the whole range, which is far too coarse to fit a piece by eye — the arrows are the fine control. The focused row is drawn with `focus_*`. SCALE IS PER-AXIS (sx/sy/sz): a garment generated separately from the body is rarely the same build, so a uniform scale can line it up but never make it fit. Scale and offset are both in WORLD axes at rest (x lateral, y depth, z up), NOT bone axes — the fit cancels the socket rest rotation, so x thickens sideways whichever bone the piece hangs off.
fit._rows_note: The gadget's rows, in panel order. SHARED CONTRACT: hud.lua lays them out and the engine cycles focus (↑/↓) and nudges (←/→) from this same list, so the order and keys cannot drift apart. `group` selects the row's min/max/nudge block above.

pocclusters._comment: flicker-pocclusters 'Cluster Editor' HUD — TWO declarative panels walked by flicker-widgets run_ui, built to the design mock (DesignSync project a39150df, 'Cluster Editor HUD.dc.html'). LEFT 'main' panel = header + mode pill, a Readout box (title + Cam/Grid/Move/Diag rows + Pick + a walk-only row + Esc hint), the 6 Debug-Overlay toggles in a 2-column grid, and a Move-speed slider. RIGHT 'inspector' panel = shown only when a face is picked: header + subtitle + a 7-column table (Corner / X Y Z local / wX wY wZ world) over the selected voxel's 8 corners. Stat + cell strings are pre-formatted in Rust (hud_model) and bound by name via text_bind; toggles + slider are two-way binds. Every colour is a $token (single palette source = this file's theme.tokens). Caps labels now carry the mock's letter-spacing (the `label` font role tracks them); numeric cells set `tracking = 0` on their text nodes so the fixed-width columns stay aligned. Corner runes ARE rendered (the `Prism Rune` face + `runes` config: each panel is a `stack` overlaying 4 Elder Futhark glyphs — top two rune-light over a feathered `rune_halo` panel, bottom two bronze). Panel headers carry a bronze ✦/◈ icon with lead/trail spacers that clear the corner runes; the Esc hint sits in a bordered `keycap`; the inspector closes with a colour-coded ◆ local / wX·wY·wZ world legend. Remaining mock flourishes a vector HUD still can't do (gem glyphs, runePulse animation, inset shadows) are omitted. The separate `hud`/`voxel` sections still serve the legacy voxel-cluster example — keep them distinct.

celestial._comment: The Celestial Cycle panel (bottom-right) — the recovered voxel.lighting controls restyled to the Prism mock. Two groups: 'Sky · the paired hands' (Sun + Moon in a box well) and 'World · independent' (Year/Speed/Fog/Latitude/Epoch), plus View toggles. Sliders bind two-way to the celestial state in its native math units (hours / weeks 0-4 / months 0-12 / degrees / years); readout strings are pre-formatted in Rust (celestial::fmt_*) and bound by val_bind. Reuses this file's theme.tokens (single palette) + the pocclusters panel/box/slider/checkbox styles.
celestial.title: $pc_celestial_cycle

chat._comment: Floating in-world comms window — the flicker-widgets `chat_panel` builder (a per-frame Rust UiNode tree the pocclusters scene runs as a SECOND run_ui pass over the HUD, so the window can move + resize; not a cached tree). Maps the DesignSync ChatPanel (MCP 36F7946B) onto the clay-chat v0.1 line protocol (MCP D9FE6CE0). Container leaves (window/titlebar/tabstrip/tab_*/log/roster/input_bar/btn*) are panel styles (fill_top/fill_bot/border/radius); *_color + line_* + roster_* are TEXT colours (a text node's dotted `color` path). `input` is the text_field style (top/bot/border/caret/placeholder/label). Single palette: every value is a $token from theme.tokens.

pocepochs._comment: Alpha/flicker-pocepochs HUD (hud_pocepochs.lua): the walker readout — title/stats/state/hints (top-left) + the LIFE-SUPPORTING CONDITIONS panel (bottom-right: 5 ui.gauge rows + the verdict light). The surface-view legend + element-distribution panels stay scene-drawn (per-element literal colours have no walker channel). Colours are $tokens where the legacy literals matched them exactly (the old habitability_hud.lua literals were authored AS mirrors of theme.tokens); the rest keep their POC values verbatim.

sablework._comment: flicker-sablework 'Sablework Bench' HUD (hud_sablework.lua) — the texture SYNTHESIZER console. Three columns: LEFT the 6-voice CHANNEL RACK (per row: on-toggle, source pill, scale/octaves/warp sliders, blend pill, amount), CENTRE the tiled swatch preview + map selector, RIGHT the OUTPUT STAGE (relief/roughness/metalness/AO) over the selected voice's fine knobs. The preview RECT lives here under `preview` and is read by BOTH the Lua (which frames it) and the Rust scene (which draws the swatch sprites into it) — one source of truth, so the frame and the image cannot drift apart. Every colour is a $token and every label a stringtable $token (the one palette + one string source).

layout._comment: The bench rides the SHARED `workbench` template (ui_templates.json) like Clayworks and Loomforge — frame + header + tab bar + [viewport | rail] + footer. These are that template's slot dimensions; the frame's own chrome comes from the default `settings` style, which is why no window colours are redefined here.

preview._comment: The swatch. `tiles` is how many times the scene repeats the baked swatch per axis BEFORE uploading, so the seam is visible in one sprite node instead of nine. The Lua sizes the well; the scene reads `tiles` to build the image. w/h square, so the tiling reads honestly.

solarbirth._comment: flicker-solarbirth HUD (hud_solarbirth.lua): the walker readout — title, flight-phase line, controls hint, and the fixed 8-planet roster legend. Roster row colours are the scene's HUD tints: each school colour with every channel floored at 0.35 (the legacy `p.color[i].max(0.35)` lightening), authored here because the walker's colour channel is dotted style paths. The ruled school colours themselves stay in flicker-orrery.

world._comment: flicker-world in-scene HUD (scripts/world_ui.lua). Was the app's local `hud` key; moved here under `world` to avoid colliding with pocclusters' `hud`.

_bucket_legacy: ══ LEGACY / EXAMPLE-ONLY ══  No prism-alpha consumer. hud + voxel = examples/voxel-cluster; sim + readout = examples/flicker-sol2 (slated for deletion). Quarantined for removal — do not build on these.

quartermaster._comment: Quartermaster Bench (flicker-quartermaster) — the content air-traffic controller: a two-tab file manager over the staging/ and package/ trees. Its tree is built in Rust (unbounded folder listings whose node ids encode positions), so this section is read by the crate directly rather than by a hud_*.lua.
quartermaster._class_comment: class.* are the DERIVED content classes (flicker_content::PackageClass::id) a row's name is coloured by — classification IS the colour, so a glance down the Name column reads as content types. A class with no entry here falls back to unknown.

rename._comment: The inline rename field. `rename_bad` is the same box with a danger rim — a name that cannot be used BLOCKS the commit and says so, rather than discarding what was typed.

pane_focused._comment: The focused pane carries a sapphire rim — on a pad this ring IS the cursor's home, so it must read at a glance.

rowsel._comment: The selection wash. Sits UNDER the row's click target, which is never gated on selection — gating it would make every unselected row unclickable.

scrim._comment: The bench's modal dim — passed to the `conflict_dialog` proto as its `overlay_style` skin. The dialog chrome itself is the proto's (modal.panel).

card._comment: One side of a collision (existing / incoming) — passed to the `conflict_dialog` proto as its `card_style` skin.

menu._comment: The focused-item context menu — the `item_context_menu` proto's default skin. Same block shape as the settings dropdown popup, so it matches the `select` popup exactly.
menu.label: $ink_button

rowsel_off._comment: The invisible full-width click/focus target over each row.
rowsel_off.label: $ink

readout._comment: flicker-sol2 top-right stats overlay (scripts/sim_ui.lua) — pure Lua text from the Model.

voxel._comment: voxel-cluster in-scene HUD (examples/voxel-cluster/scripts/hud.lua). Was the app's local `hud` key; moved here under `voxel` to avoid colliding with pocclusters' `hud`.

lighting._comment: Day/night cycle sliders, lower-right. Values flow both ways through the Model (time_of_day 0-24h, moon_phase 0-4wk, year_month 0-12mo).
